title: Garmin Connect export (raw)
description: The subset of a Garmin Connect export that packages/connectors/src/providers/garmin reads. Field names are Garmin's, not ours — this schema documents the dialect we accept at the boundary, and every field is optional because a real export is full of holes: a night without the watch produces no sleep record, a readiness entry with level NONE and no score, averageStressLevel -1, and restingHeartRate 0. Availability measured over one real 328-record export: recoveryTime 99%, bodyBattery 76%, acuteLoad 70%, readiness score 5%.

readiness.description: Garmin's daily recovery assessments. The dependable field here is recoveryTime, not score.

timestamp.description: Fallback when calendarDate is absent: ISO 8601 or epoch milliseconds.

score.description: Training Readiness 0-100. Null whenever Garmin could not compute it — most often no valid sleep record.

level.description: Garmin's own qualifier. NONE means the score is not trustworthy and must not be read as evidence.

recoveryTime.description: Minutes Garmin still considers owed before full recovery.

hrvWeeklyAverage.description: **511 is a not-established sentinel, not a millisecond figure**, the same kind of value as restingHeartRate 0 and averageStressLevel -1. Measured across 330 consecutive days of one real export (2025-10-18 to 2026-07-26, three TrainingReadinessDTO files): every day reads 511, with hrvFactorPercent 0 beside it — Garmin weighting its own HRV at nothing. A real weekly average sits in the tens of milliseconds. Never mapped to hrv_ms. The cause is a prerequisite, not a missing capability: Garmin only reports HRV status after a sustained run of nights slept wearing the watch, and in the same export validSleep is true on 4 of 330 days, never more than 2 consecutive. So 511 means the athlete could have this signal by wearing the watch to bed — which is worth saying to them, and is the opposite of what "the device cannot measure HRV" would imply. Do not infer the required run length from these files; they only show it was never approached.

dailySummaries.description: One wellness summary per calendar day.

restingHeartRate.description: 0 is Garmin's not-measured sentinel, not a heart rate.

sleep.description: Overnight sleep records. Absent entirely for any night the watch was not worn — the single largest source of missing recovery evidence.

napTimeSeconds.description: Naps are a separate window and are not counted as a night.

sleepScores.description: Withheld by Garmin when the night was timed but judged too fragmentary to score.

activityType.description: Either Garmin's {typeKey} object or the bare type key string.

beginTimestamp.description: Epoch milliseconds. Activities without it are skipped — an undated session cannot be placed on a load curve.

activityTrainingLoad.description: Garmin's EPOC-derived load. When absent the connector falls back to a duration estimate and says so via metadata.loadSource.
